description.narrative: - Projektet omfattar främjande av mänskliga rättigheter utifrån institutionella kapacitetsutvecklingsprogram genom utbildning och forskning, samt forum för och mellan viktiga nyckelintressenter, fokuserande på akademiska institutioner, aktörer inom rättsväsendet, nationella människorättsinstitutioner, samt andra uppgiftsbärare och intressenter inom olika sektorer och förvaltningsnivåer i Republiken Armenien.

- Projektet, som implementeras av Raoul Wallenbergs institut för mänskliga rättigheter och humanitär rätt, kallat «Armeniska programmet 2020-2022», omfattar tre mål, nämligen: Mål 1 – om MR-aspekter i den pågående reformprocessen inom rättsväsendet, Mål 2 – om sektorövergripande dialog i MR-frågor, Mål 3 – om MR-utbildning och forskning. Projektet är knutet till den armeniska Strategin för rättsliga och juridiska reformer för perioden 2019-2023, har ett sektorövergripande och tvärvetenskapligt angreppssätt, samt en genomförandeperiod om två år, 2020-2022.

- The project of Raoul Wallenberg Institute of Human Rights and Humanitarian Law, called «Armenia Programme 2020-2022», covers three outcomes, namely: Outcome 1 on HR aspects in the on-going justice sector reform process; Outcome 2 – on cross-sectoral dialogue on HR issues; Outcome 3 – on HR education and research. The project is linked to the draft Armenian Strategy for Judicial and Legal Reforms for the period 2019-2023, has a cross-sectoral and inter-disciplinary approach, and an implementation period of two years, 2020-2022.

Key results achieved include:
Increased cooperation with key justice sector representatives to help them integrate international human rights standards in their work
Legislative safeguards for persons engaged in human rights protection examined per international practice and local specifics and discussed with stakeholders. Proposals for legislative amendments and implementation measures to ban child corporal punishment developed and validated with relevant stakeholders. Guidelines on legal definitions of torture developed and integrated in training of judges, prosecutors, and investigators at the Academy of Justice. Human rights training delivered for selected representatives of the penitentiary service, probation service, and Ministry of Justice.
Increased dialogue between representatives of different sectors on relevant human rights issues
Dialogue on the establishment of an independent mechanism to investigate torture cases initiated with multiple stakeholders. Cooperation between legal clinics and other stakeholders, including civil society and the Human Rights Defenders Office (HRDO), initiated on human rights issues. The process to develop the next National Human Rights Action Plan (NHRAP) enhanced in collaboration with the Ministry of Justice and in coordination with UNDP.
Strengthened capacities of academia to produce and disseminate human rights knowledge through research, education and outreach
Research cooperation between academia and civil society developed on human rights issues relevant to Armenia for further discussion with respective policymakers. Revision process of MA programmes at the American University of Armenia and Yerevan State University informed by RWI recommendations.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
